title: Pages
lead: Manage structured site pages with validated content, authenticated preview and recoverable revision history.

sections.title: Create and edit
body: Open Pages → Overview, then create a page from an existing model. Use a lowercase unique slug and choose a model supported by the active template.

Edit content in Fields mode or inspect the readable JSON. Save changes only after checking required metadata and the template contract. Homepage edits are routed to Homepage when that plugin is active.

sections.title: Add components
body: Use Insert component to choose a registered plugin service and a template-supported format. The generated marker is inserted in a content section. Block markers must occupy their own paragraph.
Legacy Slides markers and typed slide blocks remain supported. Components show only data that the provider permits publicly.

sections.title: Publish and recover
body: Ordinary pages can be drafts or published. Homepage and 404 are protected published pages. Preview requires an authenticated session.
Trash preserves removable pages in revision history. Restore only from a listed revision; concurrent edits are rejected rather than overwritten.

sections.title: Shared HTML and public page data
body: The optional HTML / Mustache panel in a page editor uses the same core renderer as Homepage. Enabling it replaces the structured body view while preserving the page metadata and original structured JSON. Disable it to return to that original structure. Bind multiple public services, then write semantic HTML and loops manually. pages:list(limit:1–12) supplies items with title, text, href and image, excluding reserved home/404 pages, drafts and deleted pages.

Pages is a document source for Homepage: choose a published page by slug. The source adapter supplies its common semantic content (title, summary, facts and sections) or its authored HTML; it does not duplicate the native template frame or all template-specific extras. Editing the source updates the next request. A missing source never exposes a draft.
